documents.title: H&P - Admission - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: ADMISSION H&P
Time of eval: 22:40, HD1
CHIEF COMPLAINT: Shortness of breath and leg swelling
HPI:
88 yo female with known HFrEF (EF 35% on echo last yr per records), HTN, CKD, T2DM presents with 5 days of progressive dyspnea.
Pt reports she can no longer walk to the bathroom without stopping. Sleeping in recliner the last 2 nights.
Orthopnea requiring 3 pillows before she moved to the recliner. Denies fever, cough, chest pain.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
Daughter, who fills her pill box, confirms no missed doses. Admits to canned soup and deli meat most days.
Denies syncope. No recent med changes other than the diuretic increase.
ED COURSE:
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED with 300 mL UOP in first hour.
Foley not placed; pt able to use bedside commode with assist.
PMH:
HFrEF, HTN, CKD stage 3b, T2DM on oral agents, osteoarthritis, prior cholecystectomy.
HOME MEDS:
furosemide 80 mg PO BID, carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, spironolactone 12.5 mg daily
metformin 500 mg BID, atorvastatin 40 mg qHS, aspirin 81 mg daily, vitamin D
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash
SOCIAL: Lives with daughter. Uses rollator at baseline. Never smoked. No alcohol.
FAMILY HX: Mother with HTN. Father CAD.
ROS: Positive for DOE, leg swelling, early satiety, abdominal fullness. Negative for hemoptysis, melena, dysuria.
EXAM:
Vitals 22:50: BP 148/82, HR 96, T 36.7, RR 28, SpO2 91% on 4L NC. Wt 71.4 kg.
Gen: Elderly female, sitting upright, appears tired but not toxic.
Respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath.
Neck: JVD to angle of jaw at 45 deg. No thyromegaly.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm. S3 present. No murmur appreciated over the breath sounds.
Lungs: Bibasilar crackles to mid lung fields bilaterally. No wheeze.
Abd: Soft, mild RUQ tenderness, liver edge 2 cm below costal margin.
Ext: 3+ pitting edema to mid thigh bilaterally. Skin taut, no ulceration. Feet warm.
Neuro: Alert, oriented x3, no focal deficit.
LABS on arrival:
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago). BUN 48. K 4.1. Na 133. Bicarb 24.
WBC 7.9, Hgb 10.8, Plt 221.
Troponin 0.04 flat on repeat. Mg 1.9. TSH normal.
LFTs: AST 38, ALT 31, alk phos 112, T bili 1.2, albumin 3.3.
ASSESSMENT:
88 yo female with acute decompensated HFrEF, volume overload, hypoxemic respiratory insufficiency, and worsening renal function.
Picture is congestive rather than infectious - no fever, no leukocytosis, symmetric findings, clear volume trigger with dietary sodium.
Rising creatinine most likely cardiorenal from venous congestion rather than intravascular depletion given the exam.
PLAN:
1. Diuresis: furosemide 80 mg IV every 12 hours. Strict I/O. Daily standing weight.
2. Oxygen: continue 4L NC, wean for SpO2 greater than 92%. Head of bed up.
3. Renal: BMP q12h. Hold lisinopril and spironolactone for now. Hold metformin.
4. Continue carvedilol 6.25 mg BID - not in cardiogenic shock, warm and well perfused.
5. 2 g sodium diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction.
6. Cardiology consult requested for guidance on diuretic strategy.
7. DVT ppx: heparin 5000 units SC q8h.
8. Code status: DNR/DNI per pt and daughter, reconfirmed at bedside tonight.
Disposition: admit to stepdown.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 07:15
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt slept in bed with 3 pillows, up twice to void. Says breathing is a little easier but still winded with any effort.
Ate half of breakfast. No chest pain. Denies dizziness.
RN reports UOP 440 mL over the last 24 h despite two doses of IV diuretic.
OBJECTIVE:
Vitals: BP 138/74, HR 92, T 36.5, RR 24, SpO2 91%. Remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
Weight 70.9 kg, down 0.5 kg from admission.
I/O last 24h: in 720 mL, out 440 mL.
Exam: JVD persists to jaw. S3. Bibasilar crackles unchanged. 3+ edema to mid thigh.
Abd soft, less tender. Extremities warm.
LABS 06:05:
Creatinine 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2. BUN 56. K 3.8. Na 132. Bicarb 25.
Hgb 10.5, Plt 215.
ASSESSMENT:
Inadequate diuresis with concurrent rise in creatinine. Exam remains congested - not pre-renal. Diuretic braking.
PLAN:
1. Converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL. Bolus 80 mg IV given at drip start.
2. Hourly UOP documentation; reassess response at 6 h.
3. KCl 40 mEq PO now, recheck K this afternoon.
4. Continue 4L NC, wean as tolerated.
5. Continue to hold ACEi, MRA, metformin.
6. Cardiology at bedside - agrees with infusion strategy, will follow.
7. Continue 2 g Na diet, 1.5 L fluid restriction.
8. PT eval ordered for mobility and safety.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: PROGRESS NOTE - HD2 16:30 - interval reassessment
SUBJECTIVE:
Pt notably more comfortable. Now speaking in full sentences. Asked to sit in chair for lunch, tolerated 40 min.
Reports she voided large volumes all afternoon. No cramping, no lightheadedness on standing with assist.
OBJECTIVE:
Vitals 16:00: BP 126/70, HR 88, RR 20, SpO2 93% on 4L NC. Afebrile.
UOP since drip start 08:00: 1,850 mL brisk clear urine. Net negative 1.5 L so far today.
Weight this afternoon 69.4 kg.
Exam: JVD now to mid neck at 45 deg. Crackles at bases only. Edema 2+ to knees, skin less taut.
Lungs clearer in upper fields. No accessory muscle use at rest.
ASSESSMENT:
Good response to continuous furosemide infusion after poor response to intermittent bolus dosing. Congestion improving, oxygenation improving.
Potassium and magnesium falling as expected with brisk diuresis.
PLAN:
1. Continue furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr overnight, reassess at 06:00.
2. KCl 40 mEq PO x1 now, magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 2 h. Repeat BMP and Mg in AM.
3. Attempt oxygen wean to 3L NC this evening if SpO2 stays above 92% at rest.
4. Strict I/O, daily standing weight, target net negative 1 to 2 L per day.
5. Continue carvedilol. ACEi and MRA still held pending renal trend.
6. Watch for overshoot - hold infusion and notify if SBP under 95 or UOP over 250 mL/hr sustained.
7. PT saw pt, ambulated 30 feet with rollator, recommends continued therapy.
8. Updated daughter by phone at 16:20.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
lines: DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted HD1, discharged HD3. Length of stay 3 days.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Acute decompensated heart failure with reduced EF, volume overload
2. Acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3b, cardiorenal physiology, improving
3. Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia, corrected
4. Hypertension, T2DM
HOSPITAL COURSE:
88 yo female presented with 5 days of progressive dyspnea and leg swelling.
Cardiology clinic doubled home furosemide to 80 mg twice daily 5 days ago; patient reports adherence; weight gain of 4.5 kg over that period with worsening leg swelling.
At presentation respiratory rate 28 with accessory muscle use; speaking 3 to 4 words per breath; orthopnea requiring 3 pillows.
SpO2 86% on RA at triage; started on 4L NC with SpO2 up to 91%; remained on 4L NC through hospital day 2.
Furosemide 80 mg IV given in the ED, repeated at 80 mg IV every 12 hours; converted to furosemide infusion at 10 mg/hr on hospital day 2 for urine output under 500 mL.
Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL on arrival (baseline 1.3 mg/dL from clinic 2 months ago), 2.4 mg/dL on hospital day 2, down to 1.8 mg/dL on HD3.
Response to the infusion was brisk. Net negative 3.9 L for the admission. Discharge weight 67.6 kg, down 3.8 kg.
Oxygen weaned to room air by HD3 07:00 with SpO2 94% at rest and 92% after ambulating 100 feet.
Potassium and magnesium repleted; K 4.0 and Mg 2.1 at discharge. Infusion stopped HD3 06:00 and transitioned to oral dosing.
Lisinopril and spironolactone were held during admission. Metformin held while creatinine rising.
Cardiology followed and agrees with discharge plan and outpatient titration.
DISCHARGE EXAM: BP 124/68, HR 84, RR 18, SpO2 94% RA. JVD not elevated. Lungs clear. 1+ ankle edema. Ambulates with rollator.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
furosemide 80 mg PO BID
carvedilol 6.25 mg PO BID
atorvastatin 40 mg qHS, aspirin 81 mg daily, vitamin D
KCl 20 mEq PO daily
HOLD lisinopril and spironolactone until renal function rechecked by cardiology
HOLD metformin until BMP reviewed in clinic
INSTRUCTIONS:
2 g sodium diet - written handout given, reviewed with daughter at bedside.
1.5 L daily fluid limit. Weigh every morning after voiding, same scale, log it.
Call if weight rises 2 kg in 2 days, or with worsening breathing, or new orthopnea.
FOLLOW UP:
Cardiology in 5 days with BMP drawn that morning.
Primary care in 2 weeks. Home health RN and home PT arranged.
Code status: DNR/DNI, documented and discussed with pt and daughter.
Discharged HD3 at 14:10 with daughter, stable, ambulatory with rollator.
